title: 2013 AMC 12B Problem 6
statement: Real numbers \(x\) and \(y\) satisfy the equation \(x^2 + y^2 = 10x - 6y - 34.\) What is \(x+y?\)

solutions.text: Rearranging gives \(x^2 - 10x + 25 + y^2 + 6y + 9\) \(= 0,\) that is \((x-5)^2 + (y+3)^2 = 0.\) Hence \(x = 5\) and \(y = -3,\) so \(x + y = 2.\) Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Move every term to one side and complete the square in both \(x\) and \(y\)
A sum of two squares equal to \(0\) forces each square to be \(0\)
